text:
anya: Heads-up  quick design review: proposing a compact roles row in the invite drawer (single-line chips + a chevron to expand details). Aim: reduce vertical length and make invites faster on narrow screens. Figma: https://figma.redwood/compact-roles :link:

matt: I like compactness. Two concerns: 1) long role labels + permissions overflow, 2) discoverability of the expand affordance on mobile. Maybe add a subtle down caret and a11y hint "Press enter to expand".

rui: Accessibility: chips must be reachable via Tab and navigable with Arrow keys. When expanded, use `aria-expanded=true` and move focus into the detail region. Also announce expansion: `aria-live=polite` text like "Role details: Viewer, expanded". For truncated text add `aria-label` with full role + short permission line.

sarah: Copy notes: chip brief: "Viewer — read only". Detail panel header: "Viewer role"; body: "Can view projects, logs, and audit trails. Cannot invite or change settings." If we hide permissions behind expansion, make the teaser explicit: "Details" link.

leo: Mobile overflow pattern idea: show up to 4 chips then a "+N more" chip that opens a scrollable list. If users tap +N more often, we should consider a multi-row default on tablet.

ken: Telemetry to add: `invite.compact_row.expand`, `invite.compact_row.select`, `invite.compact_overflow_open`. Also capture `invite_time_to_complete_ms`. If compact row reduces completion by >15% we ship.

matt: Regarding SSO: if org has SSO enforcement, annotate chips with a tiny lock icon and tooltip: "SSO enforced: assignment requires linked accounts". For enforcement toggle in org settings: require typed confirm when disabling. Proposed copy in confirm modal: "Disabling SSO enforcement may allow sign-ins without your identity provider. Type your org name to confirm: <org-name>".

rui: When SSO is enabled we should still let you pick roles, but disable assign buttons for accounts not SSO-linked and show a clear tooltip "Link account to assign". Keyboard announcement for disabled control: "Cannot assign Viewer: SSO required".

anya: Audit log flow: if a role is selected from invite flow and user navigates to Audit > Entries, preserve that role as a pre-filled filter and show a small banner: "Filtered by role: Viewer (from Invite)", with "Clear filter" button. The filter chip must be keyboard dismissible via Esc when focused.

sarah: Tiny copy tweak for banner: use "Applied filter: Viewer (from Invite flow)" — clearer. Also ensure the banner includes a link to return to the invite drawer.

leo: Dev question: how to persist filter state across pages? Put it in history (URL param: `?role=viewer&src=invite`) so back/forward works. Also update breadcrumbs to show "Invites > Audit Logs" when navigated from the drawer.

matt: Visual: add an inline tag icon and subtle color to the filter pill so it reads as a state, not an action. Make sure contrast passes AA.

ken: I'll add tracking for `audit.filter_applied_from_invite` and capture device width so we can segment mobile vs desktop.

rui: Accessibility test plan: keyboard walkthrough, screen reader announcements for expand/collapse, and test mobile talkback behavior for the +N overflow. I'll write a short checklist.

design-bot: design-assets: uploaded `invite/compact-roles/v2` frames (mobile, tablet, desktop) to Figma, included overflow and SSO-annotated states. :white_check_mark:

anya: Actions:
- Rui: keyboard/a11y checklist + sample DOM snippets (due Tue EOD)
- Matt: update Figma with caret affordance + responsive multi-row fallback (due Wed)
- Sarah: finalize all microcopy and SSO confirm modal wording (legal review)
- Ken: add telemetry events to tracking board and create mobile vs desktop experiment ticket
- Leo: prototype URL param approach for filter persistence (PR spike)

matt: ack :thumbsup:

rui: starting checklist now :eyes:

sarah: pinging legal for modal copy review

ken: adding tracking spike to sprint board

anya: Thanks team  will run usability with 3 users on Thursday and iterate. :sparkles:
